cards.title: Targeting and location rules for offer differentiation
cards.summary: Use URL, geography, UTM source and cart value rules to show the right offer in the right place.
cards.use_when: Setting up pop-up targeting rules for a sitewide form, a sale form, or a channel-specific offer test.

cards.title: Master list plus engaged segments as the base setup
cards.summary: Create one master email list that all forms and checkout feed, and build engagement segments on top of it.
cards.use_when: Setting up or cleaning up your ESP account before building flows and campaigns.

cards.title: Campaigns versus flows, and stopping message overlap
cards.summary: Flows capture behaviour-triggered lifecycle revenue; campaigns capture time-sensitive moments — and the two must be coordinated.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether a recurring send should become an automation, and diagnosing high unsubscribe or spam complaint rates.

cards.title: Welcome series: trigger, filter and immediate code delivery
cards.summary: Trigger the welcome series on list addition, gate it to never-purchasers, and send the signup offer code immediately.
cards.use_when: Building your first automated welcome flow after someone subscribes via pop-up or checkout.

cards.title: Design emails outside the ESP with image slices
cards.summary: Build email creative in a design tool and slice it, so brand fonts render consistently instead of being replaced by fallbacks.
cards.use_when: Producing welcome, cart, post-purchase and campaign creative that must match your brand across devices and inboxes.

cards.title: Dynamic product feeds for emails
cards.summary: Use the ESP product block to insert static or rule-based dynamic products from your store into emails.
cards.use_when: Adding product recommendations to welcome, browse, cart or campaign emails, especially when inventory and bestsellers change often.

cards.title: Design Welcome Emails Outside Klaviyo, Export as Image Slices
cards.summary: Build welcome emails in Figma, export sliced images, and assemble them in Klaviyo for branding consistency beyond what templates allow.
cards.use_when: Designing your first welcome email for a new subscriber, where you need a branded look that Klaviyo's template/HTML editor can't produce (e.g., custom graphic placement).

cards.title: Welcome Series Content Blueprint for DTC Brands
cards.summary: Sequence five-plus welcome emails, each covering a different reason to buy, while keeping the pop-up offer visible in every email.
cards.use_when: Planning the content and sequence of your welcome flow after a subscriber joins via a pop-up offer.

cards.title: Trigger Abandoned Checkout on checkout started With Order Filtering
cards.summary: Set up the abandoned checkout flow on the checkout started metric (labeled 'abandoned cart' in Klaviyo) filtered to exclude completed orders.
cards.use_when: Building the abandoned checkout flow in Klaviyo and setting the trigger and flow filters.

cards.title: Test email and SMS sequencing in abandonment flows
cards.summary: Compare coordinated channel sequences while preserving shopper permissions, purchase exclusions and contact limits.
cards.use_when: Configuring the channel logic in an abandoned checkout or abandoned cart flow when you have both email and SMS.

cards.title: Branch Abandonment Flows by Prospect vs. Existing Customer
cards.summary: Split abandoned checkout and cart flows into first-time prospects (welcome offer, product highlights, objections) and returning customers (loyalty/subscription incentives).
cards.use_when: Writing content and setting up conditional splits inside abandoned checkout and abandoned cart flows.

cards.title: Link Abandonment Emails Directly Back to Checkout
cards.summary: Use the checkout URL event variable on images and buttons so recovery emails return each shopper to their saved checkout, not the homepage.
cards.use_when: Setting up links in abandoned checkout/cart email images and buttons so shoppers don't have to re-add products.

cards.title: Use Klaviyo Templates Only For Dynamic Cart Tables
cards.summary: Start abandonment flows from Klaviyo templates to inherit the working dynamic product table, then replace the design with your Figma-built email.
cards.use_when: Building abandoned cart, abandoned checkout, or browse abandonment emails where you need a dynamic product table but custom design.

cards.title: Fix Browse Abandonment Filters and Link to the Viewed Product
cards.summary: Add the missing added-to-cart filter to Klaviyo's browse abandonment template, then link each email to the specific viewed product, not the homepage.
cards.use_when: Setting up the browse abandonment flow for shoppers who viewed a product but took no further action.

cards.title: Design Post-Purchase Flows Around First-Time vs. Returning Customers
cards.summary: Split the placed-order flow so first-time buyers get onboarding, education, and a proactive service check-in while returning customers get loyalty and cross-sell messages.
cards.use_when: Planning the post-purchase flow that fires after an order, especially to improve first-purchase experience and repeat purchase.

cards.title: Time Your Win-Back Flow Using Actual Repurchase Data
cards.summary: Calculate median and average days between purchases, take a point in between, and delay the win-back flow to that — not Klaviyo's default 90 days.
cards.use_when: Setting the initial time delay before your customer win-back flow sends its offer emails.

cards.title: Build a Sunset Flow With a Segment Trigger and Profile Property
cards.summary: Identify unengaged subscribers with a segment, send three last-chance emails, then tag and suppress non-responders to protect deliverability and billing.
cards.use_when: Setting up the sunset flow to remove chronically unengaged subscribers from your active list.

cards.title: Set Campaign Cadence From Data, Not Ambition
cards.summary: Increase send frequency only while CTR holds and unsubscribes/spam complaints stay flat, and only to a volume you can sustain.
cards.use_when: Deciding how many campaigns per week to send for a brand roughly doing $1M–$10M/year.

cards.title: Product and Collection Spotlight Campaigns
cards.summary: Build campaign emails around one product or a thematic collection, going deep on why that specific item is best rather than listing the catalog.
cards.use_when: Choosing what to send in a weekly/regular campaign, especially for products you assume customers don't want.

cards.title: Benefit-Focused Campaigns: One Benefit Per Email
cards.summary: Isolate a single product benefit and build an entire email around it instead of listing all benefits at once.
cards.use_when: Planning campaign content when you have multiple selling points and want higher conversion from a specific customer segment.

cards.title: Use Content and Education Campaigns to Seed Purchase Intent
cards.summary: Repurpose blog/social content or teach a problem in email, then tie it back to the product you sell.
cards.use_when: Filling the campaign calendar when you don't have a promotion running, or when your product needs category education.

cards.title: Six campaign types to rotate in your email calendar
cards.summary: Pick from evergreen content, weekly newsletter, cultural event, promo (teaser/launch/last-chance/reminder) and new-product-launch campaigns based on what the store needs that week.
cards.use_when: Planning next month's campaign calendar and deciding what kind of email to send each week.

cards.title: Message and offer matter 10x more than copy polish or design
cards.summary: Prioritize what you send (product, offer, audience fit) over how beautifully you say it; a mismatched offer cannot be designed into converting.
cards.use_when: Allocating limited time between writing/designing emails and deciding what to promote and which offer to run for a campaign.

cards.title: Send campaigns to engaged segments only
cards.summary: Build a sending segment of engaged subscribers (e.g., 90-day engaged) and exclude recent buyers or other inappropriate groups, not the full list.
cards.use_when: Setting up the audience for any campaign in Klaviyo, especially new product launches or promos where some subscribers shouldn't receive it.

cards.title: Decide smart sending per campaign, not just at account level
cards.summary: Override account-level smart-sending per campaign to control whether a subscriber who just received another email gets this one.
cards.use_when: Scheduling a high-priority campaign such as a big product launch or flagship promo, and deciding whether to let smart sending hold it back.

cards.title: Set up a new-product-launch campaign in Klaviyo end to end
cards.summary: Walk-through for building, templating and scheduling a new-product-launch campaign in Klaviyo with the correct audience, template source, tracking and timing.
cards.use_when: Building and scheduling a new product launch (or similar announcement) campaign for a Shopify store.

cards.title: Add a follow-up resend to catch non-openers
cards.summary: Resend a campaign to people who didn't open the first send, with a different subject line and a narrower audience, using Klaviyo's one-click toggle or manual cloning.
cards.use_when: Maximizing reach of a high-priority campaign such as a new product launch or a time-sensitive promotion.

cards.title: Write copy that sells the click, not the product
cards.summary: For promos and launches, write email copy whose job is to get the subscriber to the website; education happens elsewhere.
cards.use_when: Writing a promo launch or new product launch email where the goal is to get subscribers clicking through to a product page.

cards.title: Write to one core message per email and cut fluff
cards.summary: Confine each email to one (at most two) overarching themes and replace paragraphs with concise, scannable copy or icons.
cards.use_when: Drafting a welcome email, campaign or any email that is drifting toward a kitchen-sink of messages.

cards.title: Lead with benefits framed for your specific customer
cards.summary: Translate product features into the benefits that matter to your named audience segment, rather than repeating product details.
cards.use_when: Writing product copy for campaigns, subscription reminders or a new product launch where the subscriber needs a reason to care.

cards.title: Subject lines and preview text: under 50 characters, frontload the value
cards.summary: Put the value in the first few words of the subject line, keep both under 50 characters, and use preview text to add detail or curiosity.
cards.use_when: Writing subject lines and preview text for any campaign where the subscriber sees only a truncated line in the inbox.

cards.title: Use persuasion levers: urgency, scarcity, social proof, curiosity gaps
cards.summary: Layer proven persuasion devices into email copy to increase the drive to act.
cards.use_when: Writing a promo, launch or content email and looking for a reliable way to increase clicks and purchases.

cards.title: Design in Figma, not in Klaviyo's drag-and-drop
cards.summary: Build emails in Figma and slice them into Klaviyo rather than designing in Klaviyo's template builder, to get clearer offer communication, stronger structure and better visuals.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to design email creative before uploading into Klaviyo for a campaign or flow.

cards.title: Structure each email section as header, subheader, body, image, CTA
cards.summary: Use a scannable section hierarchy — header, subheader, optional body copy, image and CTA — repeated per section to funnel the reader to a click.
cards.use_when: Designing a campaign or flow email layout, especially one with multiple product or content sections.

cards.title: Three visual must-do's: CTA near products, icons not bullets, clear promo code
cards.summary: Place CTAs directly under each promoted product, replace bullet points with icons, and make the promo code unmissable near the CTA.
cards.use_when: Finishing email visuals before sending a promo, collection or product-focused campaign.

cards.title: Monthly Klaviyo analytics audit: list growth, campaigns, flows
cards.summary: Run a monthly review of subscriber growth, opt-in sources and campaign performance to catch breakage and double down on what converts.
cards.use_when: The recurring monthly review of email channel performance and technical health.

cards.title: Read open rate, click rate and placed orders as a diagnostic layer stack
cards.summary: Interpret the three campaign metrics separately: open rate reflects subject line/targeting/timing, click rate reflects content and offer interest, placed orders reflect what drove purchase.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why a specific campaign over- or under-performed and deciding what to change next time.

cards.title: Use revenue and order count together to catch high-AOV distortion
cards.summary: Sorting campaigns by revenue can hide that a lower-revenue campaign drove more purchases; check placed orders and AOV before drawing conclusions.
cards.use_when: Analyzing top and bottom campaigns to decide which products, collections or campaign types to repeat.

cards.title: Diagnose a subscriber drop by separating traffic from form performance
cards.summary: When list growth falls, check whether the drop traces to site traffic decline (not controllable in Klaviyo) or form conversion decline (controllable).
cards.use_when: Monthly growth review shows a drop in new email subscribers and you need to decide whether to act on the form.

cards.title: Interpret Klaviyo's AB test statistics before trusting a result
cards.summary: Klaviyo surfaces a win probability and statistical significance but flags that test-period winners can differ from overall-send winners due to random chance, so extend or enlarge tests.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to call an A/B test campaign, subject line or flow variation a winner and roll it out.

cards.title: Read top-level business review to attribute email revenue and understand month-over-month shifts
cards.summary: Use Klaviyo's business review dashboard to see total Shopify revenue, attributed email revenue, email as a share of revenue, and the campaign vs flow split.
cards.use_when: Reporting monthly email performance to the store owner and deciding whether growth came from campaigns or flows.

cards.title: Ensure every email adds value before it ships
cards.summary: Before scheduling any campaign or turning on a flow email, confirm it educates, entertains or solves a problem for the subscriber.
cards.use_when: Final pre-send check on any campaign or flow email to catch content that has no clear subscriber benefit.

cards.title: Monthly email business review: campaign revenue decomposition
cards.summary: A repeatable month-over-month workflow for explaining why campaign revenue rose or fell by decomposing recipients, unique opens, unique clicks, conversions and AOV.
cards.use_when: Running a monthly email/retention performance review and you need to explain a revenue change rather than just report it.

cards.title: Optimize for unique opens and unique clicks, not open rate and click rate
cards.summary: The source's stated agency philosophy: drive revenue by maximizing unique opens and unique clicks, accepting lower rates when sending more volume.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to add campaign sends or widen a segment, and deciding which metrics to report on and optimize.

cards.title: Diagnose falling email metrics by which metric moved
cards.summary: A decision map that attributes declining email performance to deliverability, content, or merchandising based on which metric is falling.
cards.use_when: A monthly review shows email revenue or engagement dropping and you need to decide where to investigate first.

cards.title: Flow revenue review: traffic first, then the flow chain
cards.summary: How to review flow analytics month over month, starting with site traffic as the dominant driver and then localising the drop to a specific flow.
cards.use_when: Monthly retention review of automated flows (welcome, abandoned cart, abandoned checkout, winback) when flow revenue moved.

cards.title: Audit flow skip logic when a flow's revenue drops
cards.summary: The number-one thing the source checks when a specific flow's revenue falls is whether people are being skipped out of it by filters and triggers.
cards.use_when: A specific flow (welcome, cart, post-purchase) lost revenue month over month and you've ruled out traffic.

cards.title: Run one high-leverage campaign A/B test per month
cards.summary: Set up campaign split tests with placed order rate as the winning metric, 100% size distribution, and only one variable changed.
cards.use_when: Planning the monthly campaign experiment in Klaviyo or equivalent, and choosing what to test.

cards.title: Flow A/B tests with automatic distribution
cards.summary: Flow experiments differ from campaign tests because they run continuously, so the platform can shift traffic automatically toward the winner.
cards.use_when: Testing two versions of an email inside a flow (welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase) while the flow stays live.

cards.title: Reviewing completed and in-progress A/B tests
cards.summary: How the source decides to call a test and move on, including when to accept a high win probability without formal significance.
cards.use_when: Your monthly review of experiment results, or deciding whether to ship a variation and pick next month's test.

cards.title: Monthly deliverability health check inside Klaviyo
cards.summary: Check account-level deliverability score, the recommended thresholds, and per-mailbox-provider reports every 30 days, with clicks as the primary placement signal.
cards.use_when: Monthly email operations review, or when open/click metrics have been sliding and you suspect inbox placement.

cards.title: Recover inbox placement by tightening the engagement segment
cards.summary: When opens and clicks are steadily falling, shrink from a 90-day engaged segment to 30- or 60-day engaged, then expand again as metrics recover.
cards.use_when: Deliverability remediation: your usual engaged segment is no longer producing healthy open and click rates.

cards.title: Dynamic content blocks to merge segmented campaigns into one send
cards.summary: Use show/hide logic on content blocks so a single campaign or flow email renders different offers, copy, or reminders based on saved profile properties.
cards.use_when: You would otherwise build two near-identical campaigns for different regions, tiers, or customer states (e.g. different free-shipping thresholds, unused acquisition offer, loyalty points balance).

cards.title: Trigger a winback from expected next order date
cards.summary: Replace average-days-since-purchase winback timing with per-customer predictive date triggers so at-risk customers hear from you at their own predicted repurchase moment.
cards.use_when: Building or upgrading a winback / reactivation flow so timing is personalised rather than based on a list-wide average.

cards.title: Use predictive CLV and churn risk in flow splits
cards.summary: Apply Klaviyo's predicted analytics — next order date, churn risk, AOV, historic and predicted CLV — as branch conditions in flows rather than only reading them on profiles.
cards.use_when: Designing conditional splits in retention or winback flows to vary offer strength and personalisation by customer value.

cards.title: Build multichannel touchpoints into flows (email, SMS, push)
cards.summary: Layer SMS and push notifications into existing flows to add high-converting touchpoints at the right time, with time delays deciding channel order.
cards.use_when: Designing or upgrading an abandoned cart, abandonment, or similar conversion flow where you already have email and want more touchpoints.

cards.title: Integrate ecommerce apps to drive flow triggers and segmentation
cards.summary: Connect the Shopify apps you already use so their events and properties flow into Klaviyo and can trigger automations or refine segments.
cards.use_when: Setting up or expanding a Klaviyo account and deciding which integrations to add first.

cards.title: Trigger a birthday flow using loyalty app point properties
cards.summary: Use an integration event plus dynamic content to personalise a birthday email with the exact points earned and the customer's current balance.
cards.use_when: Running a loyalty-driven retention campaign where members earn birthday points and you want one email that renders per-customer numbers.

cards.title: Use dynamic blocks to personalise shipping thresholds and offers in one send
cards.summary: Personalise a single email's messaging, offers, and reminders using property-driven conditionals instead of splitting one audience across multiple sends.
cards.use_when: Merchandising or offer communication that differs by country, tier, or subscriber state — free shipping thresholds, unused welcome offers, loyalty balances.

cards.title: Non-discount email strategy: replace constant promos with objection-handling content
cards.summary: Build a broadcast email program that earns full-price sales by educating and handling objections instead of repeatedly discounting the whole list.
cards.use_when: Planning the overall email program for a store that currently relies on frequent sitewide discount blasts and is eroding margin.

cards.title: Send 3-4 broadcast emails per week to stay top-of-mind
cards.summary: A 3-4x weekly cadence to the engaged list is the source's tested sweet spot between irrelevance at low frequency and fatigue at high frequency.
cards.use_when: Setting or revising the sending frequency for your recurring (non-triggered) email campaigns.

cards.title: Balance broadcasts across four non-discount content pillars plus an optional sales pillar
cards.summary: Rotate educational, social proof, community/brand, and product/collection content in roughly equal amounts, with sales as a smaller optional fifth bucket.
cards.use_when: Building a monthly email content calendar and deciding what each broadcast should be about.

cards.title: Turn macro topics into hyper-specific microtopics for each email
cards.summary: Each email should deliver one narrow, single-takeaway idea rather than a broad brand message or a list of benefits.
cards.use_when: Filling calendar slots with campaign topics and writing subject lines/headlines for value emails.

cards.title: Use a two-step ChatGPT priming workflow to generate calendar ideas and copy
cards.summary: Prime the model with full brand/audience/USP context, then instruct it to output a punchy headline, sub-headline, and 2-3 sentences of body copy leading to a CTA.
cards.use_when: Generating a month of campaign ideas or drafting email copy fast, when you have brand and product context ready to feed in.

cards.title: Structure email layout as headline, sub-headline, short body, CTA, infographic, product block
cards.summary: A winning email uses a minimal, skimmable layout: headline, sub-headline, a little body copy, a CTA, an infographic/education section, then a product/CTA section at the bottom.
cards.use_when: Laying out any broadcast email before sending to design.

cards.title: Mix graphic-based and text-based emails at roughly 3-4:1
cards.summary: Blend branded graphic emails with plain-text, native-looking founder emails at about 3-4 graphic emails for every one text email.
cards.use_when: Deciding the format (graphic vs plain-text) for each send in the calendar.

cards.title: Apply the skimable, clear/concise, engaging copywriting rules
cards.summary: Write every email so it can be skimmed in seconds: no blocks of copy, one takeaway, bolded main points, and an engaging (humorous, fun, or informative) tone.
cards.use_when: Drafting or editing the body copy and headlines of any broadcast email, given short reader attention.

cards.title: Replace paragraph copy with infographics that communicate value in seconds
cards.summary: Use checklists, icon graphics, feature diagrams, timelines, numbered lists, comparison cards, tables, flowcharts, and graphs instead of dense text to convey the offer.
cards.use_when: Designing the education/benefit section of an email, or replacing a long benefits paragraph that isn't performing.

cards.title: Run plain-text vs long-form A/B tests on the same email
cards.summary: Test a short plain-text founder email against a longer ~250-word version of the same message to find what your list responds to.
cards.use_when: Optimizing a found er/community email where you're unsure whether short or longer copy converts better.

cards.title: Use sender name (not subject line) as the primary open-rate lever
cards.summary: The source argues opens are driven more by who the email is from than by the subject line, so write subject/preview text for intrigue, not for the open alone.
cards.use_when: Writing subject lines and preview text and deciding how much testing budget to spend on them.

cards.title: Keep segmentation light for broadcast campaigns
cards.summary: For manual broadcast campaigns, the source says you can send to your engaged list without heavy segmentation.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much list segmentation effort to invest in your recurring broadcast program.

cards.title: Reframe the 2024 Ecommerce Market Before Planning Funnel Spend
cards.summary: Post-2020 stimulus-era buying behavior is gone; more brands and more skeptical buyers mean acquisition-first funnels underperform unless back-end conversion is engineered.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to allocate budget and effort between cold ad acquisition and post-click email capture/retention for your store.

cards.title: Build the 'Stand a Chance' Funnel: 10% Email Capture Instead of Paying to Retarget
cards.summary: Sending cold traffic only to a purchase means paying to retarget the 99% who leave; adding a 10% email opt-in step unlocks cheap repeated content.
cards.use_when: Designing or auditing your site funnel to decide whether email capture is placed early enough to monetize cold ad traffic.

cards.title: Use the Trust Threshold Model to Justify Content Over One-Shot Ads
cards.summary: Cold visitors can only be converted after enough content exposures cross a personal trust threshold, so repeated low-cost content beats expensive single ad impressions.
cards.use_when: Deciding how many touches and what mix of ads/email a product page visitor needs before you expect a purchase.

cards.title: Win the Honeymoon Phase: Prioritize New Subscriber Capture
cards.summary: New subscribers are worth more than older ones because fresh interest and first-purchase intent peak right after opt-in.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to invest list-growth effort and how to sequence messaging for a newly opted-in shopper.

cards.title: Deploy the Four List-Growth Methods and Know Their Roles
cards.summary: Pop-up forms, post-purchase opt-ins, sign-up pages and embedded forms each capture a different traffic context, led by pop-ups converting ~10% of site traffic.
cards.use_when: Setting up or auditing all the places your store can convert traffic into email subscribers.

cards.title: Balance Flows vs Campaigns at ~50/50 of Email Revenue
cards.summary: Automated flows should carry roughly half of email revenue, and drifting far outside that band signals under-built automations.
cards.use_when: Auditing whether your automated email revenue is carrying its fair share or whether you are over-relying on manual sends.

cards.title: Run 3–4 Non-Discount Campaigns Weekly Using Microtopics
cards.summary: Send 3–4 emails per week, each built around one hyper-specific non-discount topic, to build a habit and avoid discount fatigue.
cards.use_when: Planning weekly campaign content when your list is over-exposed to sales and you need to maintain open attention without heavy discounting.

cards.title: Build a Monthly Campaign Calendar from Key Dates Outward
cards.summary: Plan each month by placing fixed sales, launches and holidays first, then adding supplementary emails and filling the gaps to hit 3–4 sends weekly.
cards.use_when: Creating next month's editorial/email calendar so campaigns are planned in advance rather than ad hoc.

cards.title: Diagnose the 9 Common Pop-Up Mistakes Killing Cost Per Acquisition
cards.summary: Most pop-ups under 1–3% because of weak offers, multi-field asks, wrong timing, slow load, small size, excess copy, unclear offers and a reflexively findable close button.
cards.use_when: Auditing an existing pop-up that is converting below target before redesigning it or testing offers.
